Hi Liam — great to hear and congrats to the team on moving ahead. Quick answers up front then a checklist of items we need:

Short summary:
- EU (Ireland): For B2B supplies to Acme Health Europe with a valid Irish VAT ID, Redwood does not charge Irish VAT on the EU line item — the transaction is typically eligible for reverse-charge and Acme will self-account. We will need a copy of the VAT certificate (or portal screenshot) and the exact billing legal entity name.
- US sales tax: Redwood collects sales tax only in states where we have legal nexus. Currently we have nexus in CA and WA; we do not collect NY or MA sales tax. If you have nexus in NY/MA and are self-billing for use tax, that is a customer responsibility.
- Canada (GST/HST): If payment originates from a Canadian office and Acme is requesting us to gross-up or withhold, we need to see the Canadian registration (BN/HST) and confirm whether the supply is taxable in Canada. Most SaaS supplies to a Canadian business are zero-rated if the customer is GST-registered and provides a valid registration number; otherwise HST may apply.

Checklist — documents we need to finalize the invoice split and to publish the correct tax footnotes on the invoice:
1) Irish VAT registration screenshot or certificate (for Acme Health Europe, confirm the exact entity/legal name).
2) US billing entity EIN + billing address for US 70% line.
3) If paying from Canada: Acme Canada BN/HST registration.
4) Preferred payment method and remittance details (ACH or wire). If wire, we’ll provide our bank details; if ACH, small verification debit may be required.

I’ll loop in Monica from Finance to prepare the split invoice template and Vivek for any contract notes related to tax clauses. Monica — can you prepare a draft split invoice and include the tax footers (reverse-charge note for EU, no NY/MA tax collected note) and attach W-9? Vivek — FYI in case legal wants special wording for self-billing.

Thanks,
